cells.tense: Right now the pull is toward many feelings at once, and you have the pen.
cells.act: work the pattern through to its logic
cells.ask: Follow one feeling you've been carrying down to its actual logic — what it asks, what follows if you take it. One feeling, worked all the way. The others keep.
cells.core:
You can feel the pull toward a dozen possible feelings without being run by it. When a structure you were standing in gives way, you don't panic; you notice what's actually there, and the pull goes quiet long enough for you to see its shape. That's the thing you do well. You gather without drowning.

Take one feeling you've been carrying and follow it down — where it actually leads, what it asks of you, what follows if you take it. Then stop there. You'll know the shape of it, and the shape is what you keep. The rest can wait their turn.

You get to see the pattern clearly, and the floor is already under you.

cells.tense: You are already bracing for a future where all of these are still open at once.
cells.ask: Keep something the last clearing produced exactly as it stands. Same shape, no reopening, no explaining it to anyone. Let it be finished.
cells.core:
When a structure gives way, the pull is to have every feeling ready at once — each one still possible, none settled, so nothing has to be missed. It feels like staying open. From inside the next week it reads as a door that keeps swinging, and the swinging is where your energy goes.

The other half of that is letting one thing stay shut. Take something the last clearing produced — a decision, a shape, a way you've started doing one thing — and keep it as it is. Don't reopen it to keep it available, and don't run it past anyone to double-check. Either it holds, or it doesn't and you find out sooner than the swinging would have shown you.

What you keep steady is what you get to keep.

cells.tense: The door cleared a while back; you are still standing where it used to be.
cells.act: let the mind rest instead of working the problem
cells.ask: Rest with nothing to solve, this afternoon or tonight. Sit or walk. If a feeling surfaces, notice it and keep going.
cells.core:
You can gather the possible feelings better than most, and the clearing that came through is still sitting behind you unread. What's absent is the rest that lets you stand inside it. The mind keeps working the problem over, so the present stays thin.

Rest with nothing to solve, this afternoon or tonight. Sit or walk. If a feeling surfaces, notice it and keep going — no working it through. Being at rest is not the answer to what you're facing; it's the ground that answer can stand on. The next look at what cleared will be steadier for it.

Nothing is being avoided by resting. Rest is what lets you arrive.

cells.tense: You are reading the pattern and calling it circumstance.
cells.act: count it out and read what the numbers show
cells.ask: Count how often a certain kind of feeling shows up when things gather around you. Just tally it. Read what the tally shows before you name it chance again.
cells.core:
You see the pattern in the feelings you gather — which one leads where, which offer costs what — and you act on what you see. Asked, you'd file it under circumstance. The reading is happening. The pen is down.

Pick one kind of feeling that keeps showing up when things gather around you, and tally it. A mark each time. No reasons, no story, no setting it up. Read the tally back a week later and see what it shows. The pattern is already running; the tally just puts a name in the author's slot.

What you see is what you're doing. The page can hold it.

attempts.check: The draft's shakiest move is telling a Too Much person that the many feelings are being kept open on purpose — the record supports bracing ahead of a future/harvest that hasn't been allowed to close, not the motive for it, so that clause is cut and the cell describes only what the gathering is doing in a recognisable moment. A reader could rightly say the collapse in this seat is happening to them, not authored by them; the Too Much ask therefore does the person's own act (hold one thing the change produced steady for a week) rather than asking them to stop gathering. The ask survives being wrong because it teaches the person something about their own pattern regardless of whether the read is accurate, and the sentence that serves the writer more than them — anything about 'the harvest of everything the heart might want' — never reaches the glass.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim I had to cut was telling a Balanced person they 'already know which one' — the record can say the pull is toward many feelings at once, not what the person has privately settled. A reader could reasonably say the clearing in this seat happened to them rather than by them, so every status now describes only what the gathering is doing in a moment they could recognise, never the motive behind it. The asks survive a wrong read because each one is the medicine's own act done small — following one feeling a step, holding one settled thing steady, an hour off, one line of consequence — and each teaches something about how they gather regardless. The sentence that served me more than them — anything about a harvest of everything the heart might want — never reaches the glass. The four asks now open on four different verbs (take, keep, give, write), two carry no clock, and none certifies what the person feels.
